chunks: Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Muhammad b. al-Marzuban narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Ja'd narrated to us. He said: Shu'ba narrated to us from Abu Imran al-Juni from Abdullah b. al-Samit. He said: Abu Dharr (may God have mercy on him) said:
I said: O Messenger of Allah! What about a man who works for himself and the people love him? He said: That is of the immediate glad tidings of the believers.

key_terms.المؤمنين: The believers; those with sincere faith
key_terms.عاجل بشرى: Immediate glad tidings; rewards that a believer receives in this world as a foretaste of the hereafter

ai.seo_question: Is it a good sign if people love you for your good deeds in Islam?
ai.summary: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari asked the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) about a person who performs righteous deeds sincerely for God and then finds that people also love and praise him for it. The Prophet reassured him that the people's love in this case is an early glad tiding (bushra) that God grants to the believer in this world, and it does not diminish the sincerity of his deed. This hadith addresses the common concern among the pious about whether others' praise invalidates one's sincerity.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Muhammad al-Marzaban narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Ja`d narrated to us. He said: Shu`ba narrated to us from Abi `Imran al-Juni from `Abdullah b. al-Samit.  He said: Abu Dharr (rh) said:
I said: O Messenger of Allah! [What do you say regarding] a man who works for himself and gains the love of the people? He said: That is of the immediate glad tidings of the believer.
